root_causes.description: An HTTP-boundary abort on payment prevents checkout's outbound gRPC call to payment from ever completing normally, so checkout blocks until its 10s deadline (checkout p99=10000ms; frontend p99=10000ms on the checkout path). Because the abort occurs at the HTTP boundary, payment emits no completed or errored server span, leaving its own server-side error_rate (0) and latency (p99~4.9ms) metrics completely normal.

evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01; a payment-side in-process fault would elevate server error spans
frontend p99 < ~200ms; only the checkout-path requests are affected

evidence.query_or_id: Updated: Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource
evidence.observed_value: Only benign flagd flag-reconciliation events on payment pods (count=1 x2); no OOMKilled/BackOff/CrashLoop

root_causes.description: A network partition isolating the payment service would likewise cause checkout's outbound gRPC call to payment to never complete, blocking until the 10s deadline while payment's own server metrics stay normal (no received spans). This cannot be fully separated from http_abort with the signals collected, but no NetworkPolicy/partition-specific events were observed.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate=0.000 with no received server spans reflected
p99=10000ms (deadline reached), consistent with unreachable downstream

root_causes.description: A payment pod crash/restart would break the checkout→payment call, but K8s events show no OOMKilled, BackOff, or CrashLoop events on payment pods, and payment server spans continue to be reported normally, making this hypothesis unlikely.

evidence.query_or_id: Updated: Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource
evidence.observed_value: No OOMKilled/BackOff/CrashLoop events on payment pods in last 600s

remediation_steps: Disable / roll back the flagd flag injecting the http_abort fault on the payment service to restore normal HTTP responses.
Restart the payment deployment pods to clear any stuck/aborted connection state and re-establish checkout→payment gRPC channels.
Verify checkout server p99 latency returns to < ~100ms and frontend p99 normalizes (currently pinned at the 10s deadline).
If the fault is instead a network boundary fault, inspect/remove any NetworkPolicy or partition injection isolating payment pods and confirm parity with the flagd flag configuration.
